record.title: Archer–Geary conjecture on chain-avoiding permutations
record.statement:
Let $C_n(231,1432: 231)$ be the set of permutations in $S_n$ that avoid the chain $(231,1432: 231)$, and let $c_n(231,1432: 231)$ denote its cardinality. Thus, the permutation avoids both $231$ and $1432$, while its square avoids $231$. Let $L_{n+1}$ denote the $(n+1)$-th Lucas number. **Archer–Geary's conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$,

$$
c_n(231,1432: 231)=L_{n+1}-\left\lceil \frac{n}{2}\right\rceil-1.
$$

This conjecture concerns the enumeration of permutations satisfying simultaneous pattern-avoidance conditions on a permutation and its square. The source attributes it to Archer and Geary; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Junyao Pan and Pengfei Guo, “On the permutations that strongly avoid the pattern 312 or 231”, arXiv:2404.01597 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01597

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Fiori's explicit two-sided conjecture for the least prime in an arithmetic progression
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $a<n$ satisfy $\operatorname{gcd}(a,n)=1$, and define

$$
P(n,a)=\min\{p\mid p\text{ is prime and }p\equiv a\pmod n\},
$$

$$
P(n)=\max_{(a,n)=1}P(n,a),
$$

where $\phi$ denotes Euler's totient function. **Fiori's explicit two-sided conjecture.** For all $n>3$,

$$
P(n)<3\phi(n)\log(n)\log(\phi(n)),
$$

and for all $n>570$,

$$
P(n)>0.5\phi(n)\log(n)\log(\phi(n)).
$$

This combines the paper's proposed explicit upper and lower bounds and is supported by the computations and outlier heuristics described there; no proof is supplied.
record.source_name: Andrew Fiori, “The Least Prime in Arithmetic an Progression”, arXiv:2404.02329 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02329

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Equivariant degree-one injectivity for braid-matroid Varchenko–Gelfand duals
record.statement:
Let $cmathcal{M}=cmathrm{Br}_n$ be the braid oriented matroid, and let $cmathrm{VG}(cmathrm{Br}_n)^!_i$ denote the degree-$i$ component of its Koszul dual. Let $cmathcal{S}_{cmathrm{VG}}(m,n-1)$ denote the corresponding $cmathfrak{S}_n$-representation.

**Braid-matroid equivariant injectivity conjecture.** For all $i
eggeq 1$, there exist equivariant injections

$$
[cmathcal{S}_{cmathrm{VG}}((n-1)+i,n-1)]=[cmathrm{VG}(cmathrm{Br}_n)^!_i]
\hookrightarrow
[cmathcal{S}_{cmathrm{VG}}((n-1)+i+1,n-1)]=[cmathrm{VG}(cmathrm{Br}_n)^!_{i+1}].
$$

Known degree-two injections exist generally for oriented matroids, but degree-one equivariant injections need not. Computations for $n
egleq 10$ and $1
egleq i
egleq 9$ support this braid-matroid claim; a proof is not supplied.
record.source_name: Ayah Almousa, Victor Reiner and Sheila Sundaram, “Koszulity, supersolvability, and Stirling representations”, arXiv:2404.10858 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2003–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0306013](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306013).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10858

record.title: Two-generation conjecture for traceless matrices over the binary field
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $\operatorname{\mathfrak{sl}}_n(\mathbf{F}_2)$ denote the Lie algebra of traceless $n\times n$ matrices over the field with two elements.

**Two-generation conjecture.** If $n \neq 4$, then $\operatorname{\mathfrak{sl}}_n(\mathbf{F}_2)$ is $2$-generated.

The authors report that random computer searches found generating pairs for every $n\leq 20$ except $n=4$, motivating the conjecture. The statement concerns the unresolved even-characteristic case; the context provided does not establish it for all $n$ or explain the exceptional case $n=4$.
record.source_name: Omer Cantor, Urban Jezernik and Andoni Zozaya, “Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields”, arXiv:2404.11240 (2025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.11240

record.title: The folklore local-to-global conjecture for cubic hypersurfaces
record.statement:
Let $X\subset \mathbf{P}_{\mathbf{Q}}^{n-1}$ be a cubic hypersurface with $n\geqslant 10$. The existence of points over every completion is necessary for a rational point, and in this range the real condition is automatic for a cubic form.

**Folklore local-to-global conjecture.** If $X(\mathbf{Q}_p)\neq\emptyset$ for every prime $p$, then

$$
X(\mathbf{Q})\neq\emptyset.
$$

Demyanov and Lewis proved the local conditions at every prime when $n\geqslant 10$, but the asserted global conclusion remains unresolved; the conjecture is the Hasse-principle expectation for cubic hypersurfaces in this range.
record.source_name: V. Vinay Kumaraswamy and Nick Rome, “On a conjecture of Wooley and lower bounds for cubic hypersurfaces”, arXiv:2405.04234 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04234

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2024). “Although Conjecture is still unresolved, the circle method has been used to make partial progress.”

record.title: Existence conjecture for maximal Tjurina curves and line arrangements
record.statement:
Let $C:f=0$ be a reduced plane curve of degree $d$, let $r={\rm mdr}(f)$, and suppose $d/2\leq r\leq d-1$. A **maximal Tjurina curve of type** $(d,r)$ is one satisfying

$$
\tau(C)=(d-1)^2-r(d-r-1)-\binom{2r+2-d}{2}.
$$

**Maximal Tjurina existence conjecture.** For every integer $d\geq 3$ and every integer $r$ with $d/2\leq r\leq d-1$, there are maximal Tjurina curves of type $(d,r)$. Moreover, for $d/2\leq r\leq d-2$, there are maximal Tjurina line arrangements of type $(d,r)$.

The conjecture is known for many pairs $(d,r)$, in particular for all relevant pairs with $d\leq 11$, but the general case remains open. The constructions include line arrangements and irreducible curves with notable geometry, such as maximal nodal curves when $r=d-1$.
record.source_name: Alexandru Dimca and Gabriel Sticlaru, “Curves with Jacobian syzygies of the same degree”, arXiv:2405.06269 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1908.06885](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.06885).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.06269

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: The common-bound conjecture for P-stable degree-sequence families
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be a P-stable family of degree sequences, or a P-stable simple region, and let $\partial(D)$ denote the boundary of a graphic degree sequence $D\in\mathbb{D}$. Let $|D|$ denote the size of $D$. **Common-bound conjecture.** There is a polynomial $p^*(n)$ such that, for each such P-stable family $\mathbb{D}$, or just for each P-stable simple region $\mathbb{D}$, 
$$
\partial(D)\le p^*(|D|)
$$
 for all but finitely many graphic $D\in\mathbb{D}$. The conjecture proposes a uniform polynomial bound on the boundary quantity for P-stable regions; the surrounding discussion notes empirical evidence for the candidate polynomial $p_0(n)=n^{10}$, but does not establish the conjecture.
record.source_name: Péter L. Erdős, István Miklós and Lajos Soukup, “Fully graphic degree sequences and P-stable degree sequences”, arXiv:2405.12013 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12013

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: Regularity extensions of Pyber, Cameron and Vdovin's conjectures
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group with a core-free maximal subgroup, and let $m(G)$ be the minimal index of a core-free maximal subgroup. Let $R_{\rm max}(G)$, $R_{\rm ns}(G)$ and $R_{\rm sol}(G)$ be the corresponding regularity invariants. **Regularity conjectures.**

$$
R_{\rm max}(G)\leqslant c\log_{m(G)}|G|
$$

for an absolute constant $c$; $R_{\rm ns}(G)\leqslant 7$ for every finite almost simple group $G$, with equality if and only if $G={\rm M}_{24}$; and $R_{\rm sol}(G)\leqslant 5$ for every finite group $G$ with trivial soluble radical. These are proposed natural extensions of the preceding base-size conjectures; the supplied text records partial results and special cases, but does not establish resolution of the full three-part proposal.
record.source_name: Marina Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Timothy C. Burness, “On the regularity number of a finite group and other base-related invariants”, arXiv:2405.15300 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15300

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: Eventual soluble regularity-two conjecture for symmetric and alternating groups
record.statement:
Let $R_{\rm sol}(G)$ denote the regularity invariant obtained by restricting to soluble subgroups. **Eventual soluble regularity-two conjecture.**

$$
R_{\rm sol}(S_n)=R_{\rm sol}(A_n)=2
$$

for all sufficiently large $n$. This is presented as a stronger conjecture in the symmetric and alternating group setting. Computations verify related cases, including the value for $n\geqslant 21$, but the general assertion for all sufficiently large $n$ remains open.
record.source_name: Marina Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Timothy C. Burness, “On the regularity number of a finite group and other base-related invariants”, arXiv:2405.15300 (2024).

record.title: Conjecture on projective special linear and unitary Miyamoto groups over prime fields
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a prime field, let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\psi\in F$ be parameters, and let $\tau_a,\tau_b,\tau_c$ be the corresponding Miyamoto involutions. Define

$$
T=\langle\tau_a,\tau_b,\tau_c\rangle.
$$

**Projective-group conjecture.** There exist parameters $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\psi\in F$ such that $T\simeq PSL(3,F)$, and a different set of parameters such that $T\simeq PSU(3,F)$. The preceding computations provide examples over the prime fields of orders $7$, $11$, and $13$ for both families, motivating the proposed existence statement for every prime field.
record.source_name: Vsevolod A. Afanasev, “Searching for groups related to pseudo-composition algebras”, arXiv:2405.15900 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15900

record.title: Malkevitch's consecutive-cycle conjecture for 4-connected planar graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a 4-connected planar graph on $n$ vertices. A cycle of length $4$ is a cycle with four vertices. **Malkevitch's conjecture.** If $G$ contains a cycle of length $4$, then $G$ contains a cycle of length $\ell$ for every $\ell\in\{n,n-1,\ldots,3\}$. This conjecture concerns cycles of consecutive lengths; the source presents it as posed by Malkevitch in 1988 and does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Ping Xu, Huiqiu Lin and Longfei Fang, “Long cycles and spectral radii in planar graphs”, arXiv:2405.20766 (2024).

record.title: Federici's conjecture on finite geodetic Cayley graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\Sigma$ be a generating set. The undirected Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(G,\Sigma)$ has vertex set $G$ and edges joining $g$ to $ga$ for $a\in\Sigma$; it is **geodetic** if every pair of vertices is joined by a unique shortest path. **Federici's conjecture.** Every finite geodetic Cayley graph is either a cycle of odd length or a complete graph. This conjecture is the central classification question studied in the paper; the paper reports verification for all groups of order at most $1024$ and for several infinite families, but does not establish the claim in full generality.
record.source_name: Murray Elder, Adam Piggott, Florian Stober, Alexander Thumm and Armin Weiß, “Finite groups with geodetic Cayley graphs”, arXiv:2406.00261 (2025).

record.title: Existence conjecture for elliptic curves and imaginary quadratic fields at large primes
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime. For an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ and an imaginary quadratic field $K_0$, consider the triple $(E,K_0,p)$ and the conditions of the source's density lemma for constructing imaginary quadratic fields with the stated Hilbert-tenth property.

**Large-prime existence conjecture.** For all sufficiently large primes $p$, there exist an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ and an imaginary quadratic field $K_0$ such that the triple $(E,K_0,p)$ satisfies all the conditions of that density lemma.

The conjecture is motivated by explicit examples for $p=11,13,31,37$, which yield positive-density results. No resolution is given for all sufficiently large primes.
record.source_name: Katharina Müller and Anwesh Ray, “Hilbert's tenth problem for families of Z_p -extensions of imaginary quadratic fields”, arXiv:2406.01443 (2024).

record.title: Pólya functional bounds for bounded convex planar domains
record.statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded convex planar domain. Let $T(D)$ denote its torsional rigidity, let $\lambda_1(D)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta_D$, and define the **Pólya functional** by

$$
F(D)=\frac{\lambda_1(D)T(D)}{|D|}.
$$

**Pólya functional bounds conjecture.** For every bounded convex planar domain $D$,

$$
\frac{\pi^2}{24}<F(D)<\frac{\pi^2}{12},
$$

and both bounds are sharp. The lower bound is approached by a collapsing sequence of isosceles triangles converging to an interval, while the upper bound is approached by elongating rectangles converging to the infinite strip. This conjecture remains open even for triangles.
record.source_name: Rodrigo Bañuelos and Phanuel Mariano, “On a conjecture of a Pólya functional for triangles and rectangles”, arXiv:2406.01778 (2024).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1203.2344](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.2344), [arXiv:1108.1524](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.1524).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01778

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2024). “Remarkably, the conjecture remains open even within the class of triangles.”

record.title: Antichain-indicator symmetry conjecture for odd uniform self-dual fences
record.statement:
Let $a$ be a positive integer, let $t$ be odd, and let $F=\breve{F}(a^t)$ be the uniform self-dual fence with $t$ segments. For $i\in\{1,\ldots,t-1\}$, let $s_i$ and $s_{t-i}$ be the corresponding shared elements, and let $\chi_{s_i}$ and $\chi_{s_{t-i}}$ be their antichain indicator statistics. **Antichain symmetry conjecture.** For every $i\in\{1,\ldots,t-1\}$, the statistic

$$
\chi_{s_i}-\chi_{s_{t-i}}
$$

is 0-mesic under rowmotion.

The authors state that this stronger conjecture was confirmed computationally for $a+t\leq 10$, for $F=\breve{F}(2^9)$, and for $F=\breve{F}(8^3)$.
record.source_name: Alec Mertin and Svetlana Poznanović, “Toggleability Spaces of Fences”, arXiv:2406.02493 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02493

record.title: The Hasse-pair coverage conjecture
record.statement:
A pair of prime powers $(q_1,q_2)$ is a **Hasse pair** when

$$
\lvert\sqrt{q_1}-\sqrt{q_2}\rvert\leq 1.
$$

If both prime powers are odd, it is an odd Hasse pair. **Hasse-pair coverage conjecture.** Every prime power is a member of some Hasse pair, and every odd prime power is a member of some odd Hasse pair. The conjecture is known to hold for all prime powers below $10^{19}$ and is intimately connected with Andrica's conjecture; its general validity remains open.
record.source_name: Eleni Agathocleous, Antoine Joux and Daniele Taufer, “Elliptic curves over Hasse pairs”, arXiv:2406.03399 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03399

record.title: Conjecture on the expected number of descents in squared permutations
record.statement:
For $n\geq 3$, let $\pi$ range uniformly over the symmetric group ${\mathcal S}_n$, and let $\operatorname{des}(\pi^2)$ denote the number of descents of the square of $\pi$. **The expected-descent conjecture.** The expected number of descents in $\pi^2$ is

$$
\mathbb{E}_{\pi\in{\mathcal S}_n}\bigl[\operatorname{des}(\pi^2)\bigr]=\frac{n-1}{2}-\frac{2}{n}.
$$

The formula is supported in the source by the tabulated values for $2\leq n\leq 10$, but no proof or resolution is supplied, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Kassie Archer and Aaron Geary, “Descents in powers of permutations”, arXiv:2406.09369 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09369

record.title: e-log-concavity conjecture for chromatic quasisymmetric functions
record.statement:
Let $G=([n],E)$ be a natural unit interval graph, and write

$$
X_G(\bm x;q)=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(q)e_\lambda.
$$

A polynomial $c_\lambda(q)$ with coefficients $a_\ell$ is **$e$-log-concave** when its coefficients satisfy $a_\ell^2\geq a_{\ell+1}a_{\ell-1}$ for every relevant index $\ell$.

**$e$-log-concavity conjecture.** Let $G$ be a natural unit interval graph. Then $X_G(\bm x;q)$ is $e$-log-concave.

This is proposed as a strengthening of $e$-unimodality. The source reports computer verification for every natural unit interval graph with at most $10$ vertices, but no general proof.
record.source_name: Bruce E. Sagan and Foster Tom, “Chromatic symmetric functions and change of basis”, arXiv:2407.06155 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06155

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

record.title: Rationality conjecture for generating functions of 231- and 312-avoiding permutations
record.statement:
For a pattern $\sigma\in\{231,312\}$, let $F_\sigma^k(x)$ be the generating function associated with pattern-avoiding permutations fixed by the $k$th iterate of the fundamental bijection. The conjecture is that, for every $k$, $F_\sigma^k(x)$ is rational:

**Rationality conjecture.** For $\sigma\in\{231,312\}$, the generating functions $F_\sigma^k(x)$ are rational. The paper gives the conjectured examples

$$
F_\sigma^3(x)=\frac{1}{1-x-x^2-2x^3},\qquad F_\sigma^4(x)=\frac{1}{1-x-x^2-2x^4-x^5-x^6},\qquad F_\sigma^5(x)=\frac{1}{1-x-x^2}.
$$

The claim concerns rationality of the generating functions for these two pattern classes; the displayed cases are examples rather than a separate general assertion.
record.source_name: Kassie Archer and Robert P. Laudone, “Pattern avoidance and the fundamental bijection”, arXiv:2407.06338 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06338

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

record.title: Sun's finiteness conjecture for exceptional determinant primes
record.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive odd integer, and define

$$
E_2(m)=\{p:p\text{ is a prime with }4\mid p-1\text{ and }p\mid S_{m+\frac{p-1}{2},2}(-1,p)\}.
$$

Here $S_{n,2}(d,p)$ is the determinant considered in the paper. **Sun's finiteness conjecture.** For every positive odd integer $m$, the set $E_2(m)$ is finite. In particular,

$$
E_2(5)=\{29\},\quad E_2(7)=\{13,53\},\quad E_2(9)=\{13,17,29\},
$$

$$
E_2(11)=\{17,29\},\quad E_2(13)=\{17,109,401\}.
$$

The displayed finite sets were supplied by Sun from calculations for primes below $1000$. The general finiteness assertion remains unresolved according to the supplied text.
record.source_name: Rituparna Chaliha and Gautam Kalita, “On some conjectural determinants of Sun involving residues”, arXiv:2407.07085 (2024).

record.title: Unimodality conjecture for matching polytopes of wheel graphs
record.statement:
Let $W_n$ be the wheel graph on $n$ vertices, with $n\geq 4$, and let $P_M(W_n)$ denote its matching polytope. The coefficients of the $h^*$-polynomial of $P_M(W_n)$ form its $h^*$-vector.

**Unimodality conjecture.** The $h^*$-vector of $P_M(W_n)$ is unimodal for every $n\geq 4$.

This conjecture is motivated by the unimodality of the computed $h^*$-vectors for $n=4,\dots,10$ and by the question of whether IDP polytopes have unimodal $h^*$-polynomials. The paper does not resolve it, and the broader question remains open.
record.source_name: Benjamin Eisley, Koji Matsushita and Andrés R. Vindas-Meléndez, “Matching polytopes, Gorensteinness, and the integer decomposition property”, arXiv:2407.08820 (2024).

record.title: Conjecture on outlier traps under $\Lambda$-poisedness
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Y}$ be the set of experimental points, and let $y^1,y^2,y^3\in\mathcal{Y}$. A point is called **bad under $\Lambda$-poisedness** when it satisfies the paper's bad-point criterion for $\Lambda$-poisedness. **Outlier-trap conjecture.** For every $y^4\in\mathcal{Y}\backslash\{y^1,y^2,y^3\}$, if

$$
\lVert y^i-y^4\rVert>2\quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,2,3\},
$$

then there is at least one $y^5\in\{y\in\mathcal{Y}\mid\lVert y-y^4\rVert\leq2\}$ that is bad under $\Lambda$-poisedness. The conjecture formalizes the experimentally observed association between distant outliers and nearby bad points under $\Lambda$-poisedness; the paper reports that more than $99\%$ of the relevant experimental points were outlier traps, but does not establish the assertion theoretically.
record.source_name: Qi Zhang and Pengcheng Xie, “On the Relationship between Λ-poisedness in Derivative-Free Optimization and Outliers in Local Outlier Factor”, arXiv:2407.17529 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.17529

record.title: Fejes Tóth's sausage conjecture for TS-packings of unit balls
record.statement:
Let $N>1$ and $3\leq d\leq 41$. Consider an arbitrary TS-packing of $N$ unit balls in $\mathbb{E}^d$. **Fejes Tóth's sausage conjecture.** The volume of their convex hull is at least the volume of the convex hull of $N$ non-overlapping unit balls whose centers lie on a line segment of length $2(N-1)$.

This asks whether the linear packing, or sausage, minimizes the convex-hull volume among TS-packings in the remaining dimensions. The claim is stated as already proved for $d=2$ and, via Betke and Henk's result, for all $d\geq 42$; the dimensions $3\leq d\leq 41$ remain under consideration.
record.source_name: Károly Bezdek and Zsolt Lángi, “On separability in discrete geometry”, arXiv:2407.20169 (2025).

record.title: Odd-indexed generalized Gauss polynomial conjecture
record.statement:
For integers $n\ge 0$ and $d\ge 1$, define

$$
G_{d,n}(q,z):=\frac{(z^{d+1}q^{(d+1)(1-n)};q^{2(d+1)})_n}{(zq^{1-n};q^2)_n}.
$$
 Here $\mathscr{U}_{q,z}^2$ denotes the class used in the paper for the relevant two-variable unimodality property. **Odd-indexed generalized Gauss polynomial conjecture.** For any odd integer $k>1$, one has

$$
G_{k,n}(q,z)\in \mathscr{U}_{q,z}^2
$$

for all $n\ge 0$. This would imply the unimodality of Andrews's generalized rank Gauss polynomials for odd $k$; the claim is supported by computations for $k\in\{3,5,7,9,11\}$ and $n\le 10$.
record.source_name: Nian Hong Zhou, “Unimodality and certain bivariate formal Laurent series”, arXiv:2408.04433 (2025).

record.title: Unimodality conjecture for refined plane-partition Betti numbers
record.statement:
For integers $n\ge 0$ and $\delta\in\frac12\mathbb Z$, let

$$
b_\delta(\ell,n)=\#\{\pi\in\mathrm{PP}: w(\pi)=n,\; w_-(\pi)-w_+(\pi)+\delta w_0(\pi)=\ell\},
$$

where $\mathrm{PP}$ is the set of plane partitions and $w_-$, $w_0$, and $w_+$ are the sums of the entries strictly below, on, and strictly above the diagonal, respectively. **Unimodality conjecture for refined plane-partition Betti numbers.** The sequences

$$
\bigl(b_0(m,n)\bigr)_{m\in\mathbb Z}
$$

are unimodal for all integers $n\ge 0$. The result is known computationally for all $n\le 30$, while the paper also establishes parity unimodality; the full unimodality remains conjectural.
record.source_name: Nian Hong Zhou, “Unimodality and certain bivariate formal Laurent series”, arXiv:2408.04433 (2025).

record.title: The finite-list conjecture for 5-vertex-critical co-gem-free graphs
record.statement:
A graph is **$5$-vertex-critical** if it has chromatic number $5$ and deleting any vertex lowers its chromatic number; a graph is **co-gem-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to the complement of the gem. The paper reports a list of 327 such graphs.

**Finite-list conjecture.** There are only finitely many $5$-vertex-critical co-gem-free graphs, and the list of 327 is complete.

The finiteness of $k$-vertex-critical co-gem-free graphs is stated to remain open for all $k\geq 5$. The list was generated computationally for graphs of order at most 18, with no examples of order 13 through 18.

record.title: Leech-lattice conjecture for quantum paving in dimension 24
record.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a Leech lattice in phase space of dimension $24$, with arbitrary fixed density greater than $1$. The **Leech-lattice conjecture.** There exists a Leech lattice that solves the quantum paving problem. The claim is motivated by the Leech lattice's optimality for sphere packing, universal optimality for energy minimization, and strong known covering properties, but it remains open; the relevant lattice may require a suitable permutation of the base vectors or rotation, rather than being the standard realization.

record.title: Non-collapse of the spectral sequence for strongly invertible knots
record.statement:
Let $\widetilde{K}$ be a strongly invertible knot, and consider the spectral sequence of Theorem 1. To say that it collapses on the $E_k$ page means that the pages agree from that page onward.

**Spectral-sequence non-collapse conjecture.** There exists a strongly invertible knot $\widetilde{K}$ such that the spectral sequence of Theorem 1 collapses on the $E_k$ page for some $k\ge 3$.

The paper notes that the spectral sequence collapses on the $E_2$ page for all strongly invertible knots with at most $11$ crossings, and conjectures that this is not the general behavior. The existence of an example requiring a later page remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Asymptotic Briggs inequalities for regular partitions and overpartitions
record.statement: Let $p_k(n)$ and $\overline{p}_k(n)$ denote the $k$-regular partition and $k$-regular overpartition functions, respectively, and let the inequalities referred to in the source as (p_kmain) and (opk-main) be the corresponding Briggs inequalities. **The conjecture.** For every positive integer $k\geq 2$, there exists $N(k)$ such that both inequalities hold for all $n\geq N(k)$. The paper proves the claim in certain ranges of $k$ and discusses computational evidence for $2\leq k\leq 100$, but the supplied text does not establish the conjecture for every $k$.

record.title: The eigenvalue-form conjecture for the substitution matrix
record.statement:
Let $n$ be odd with $n\geq 5$, let $M_n$ be the substitution matrix, and let $s_{n,j}$ denote the edge lengths used in the construction, with $0\leq j\leq (n-1)/2$. The observed roots of the characteristic polynomial $p_n(x)$ are

$$
\mu_n=\frac{1}{s_{n,(n-1)/2}},-\frac{1}{s_{n,(n-3)/2}},\ldots,\frac{1}{s_{n,2}},-\frac{1}{s_{n,1}},\frac{1}{s_{n,0}}=1.
$$

**Eigenvalue-form conjecture.** Every eigenvalue of $M_n$ has the form $\pm\frac{1}{s_{n,j}}$ for all odd $n\geq 5$. If this holds and $g_n(x)$ is irreducible for odd $n\geq 11$, then $\mu_n$ is non-Pisot, because $\frac{1}{s_{n,(n-3)/2}}=\frac{1}{2\sin(3\pi/2n)}>1$.

record.title: The product-structure conjecture above the independent-crossing threshold
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $s(n)$ be the threshold defined in the paper, and let $\alpha$ be a parameter. Consider the class of intersection graphs of $\alpha$-free homothetic regular $n$-gons.

**The above-threshold product-structure conjecture.** For every $\alpha \geq s(n)$, the class of intersection graphs of $\alpha$-free homothetic regular $n$-gons has product structure.

For $\alpha\geq s(n)$, the paper proves that the canonical drawings are $k$-independent crossing with $k=26(n+1)$. The assertion would follow from the conjectured product structure for all $k$-independent crossing graph classes.

record.title: The uniform-slicing conjecture for alphabet-multiplier upcycles
record.statement:
Let $v$ be an upcycle constructed by the alphabet multiplier theorem from an upcycle $u$ and multiplier $k$. Let $n$ and $d$ be the parameters in that construction. Slicing $v$ into cyclic partial words of a specified common length, with the slicing allowed to start at any index, produces a collection of partial words.

**Uniform-slicing conjecture.** For every $0\leq i\leq n-d$, if the slicing length is $k^i|u|$, then the resulting collection is an upfamily.

This is presented as a stronger conjecture than the existence claim above. The paper reports computational verification for the upcycle $001\mathord{\diamond}110\mathord{\diamond}$ with multipliers $k=2,3,4,5$, while the general assertion remains unresolved.

record.title: The symmetric-group conjecture for groups generated by horizontal class transpositions
record.statement:
Let $CT_{(k)}$ be the group generated by the subgroups $CT_2,CT_3,\ldots,CT_k$, where each $CT_j$ is isomorphic to the permutation group $S_j$. Let $N$ be the least common multiple of the numbers $2,3,\ldots,k$.

**Symmetric-group conjecture.** For $k>3$, the group $CT_{(k)}$ is isomorphic to the permutation group $S_N$.

This conjecture is motivated by computations in GAP, including the cases $\langle CT_2,CT_3,CT_4\rangle\cong S_{12}$ and other examples whose orders agree with the corresponding factorials. Its general validity for all $k>3$ remains open.

record.title: Conjecture on the chromatic–cochromatic gap in random graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be sampled from the binomial random graph model $G_{n,1/2}$, and let $
u$ denote the chromatic number of $G$ and $\bar\chi$ its cochromatic number, so that the gap is $\nu-\bar\chi$. Here, $f(n)=\Theta(n/\log^3 n)$ means that there are positive constants bounding the ratio between the gap and $n/\log^3 n$ for all sufficiently large $n$. **Chromatic–cochromatic gap conjecture.** With high probability,

$$
\chi(G)-\zeta(G)=\Theta(n/\log^3 n).
$$

The conjecture predicts the asymptotically sharp order of the difference between the chromatic and cochromatic numbers of a random graph. The paper proves a weaker lower bound of $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ for roughly $95\%$ of values of $n$ and conjectures that the stated order holds for all $n$.
record.source_name: Annika Heckel, “The difference between the chromatic and the cochromatic number of a random graph”, arXiv:2409.17614 (2025).

record.title: Primitive-point conjecture for the unit sphere over finite fields
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power with $q>25$, and let

$$
x^2+y^2+z^2=1
$$

be the unit sphere over ${\mathbb F}_q$. An ${\mathbb F}_q$-primitive point is a point on this sphere whose coordinates generate the extension required by the paper's definition of primitivity. **Primitive-point conjecture.** There exists an ${\mathbb F}_q$-primitive point on the unit sphere. The conjecture is motivated by computations, which found such points for all tested values of $q$ except $q=3,5,9,13,25$; the asserted existence for every prime power $q>25$ remains open.

record.title: Orthotope sum conjecture for Z-curve subsets
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{T}\subset\mathbf{X}^D_K$ be a subset, and let $\mathcal{O}\subset\mathbb{T}$ be an $D$-dimensional orthotope with $2^D$ elements. Write $S(\mathcal{O})$ for the sum of the elements of $\mathcal{O}$, and let $\Psi$ be the constant associated with the ambient set.

**Orthotope sum conjecture.** For every orthotope $\mathcal{O}\subset\mathbb{T}$,

$$
S(\mathcal{O})=\Psi.
$$

The source supports the claim with an explicit decomposition of a $48$-element subset into six orthotopes in dimension $3$, each having sum $\Psi^3_5=131068$, but supplies no general proof or resolution.

record.title: Unboundedness and surjectivity conjecture for corresponding-sequence lengths
record.statement:
Let $T(n)$ denote the minimal length of a corresponding sequence for $n$, where $n$ is a non-negative integer.

**Unboundedness and surjectivity conjecture.** The function $T(n)$ is unbounded. Moreover, it is surjective onto the set of positive integers other than $2$.

The conjecture is motivated by examples realizing every length $t\leq 14$ except $t=2$, together with computer verification that $T(n)<15$ for all $n\leq 10000$.

record.title: Stinson's strong starter conjecture for cyclic groups
record.statement: Let $n\geq 5$ be an odd integer. A **strong starter** in the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is a starter satisfying the additional distinct nonzero pair-sum condition defined in the paper. **Stinson's conjecture.** There exists a strong starter in $\mathbb{Z}_n$ if and only if $n\neq 5,9$. The cases $n=5$ and $n=9$ are known exceptions, while existence was proved for every odd $n\neq 9$ with $7\leq n\leq 99$; the general cyclic case remains open.

record.title: Conjecture for the extended irregular domination number of paths
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, and let $\gamma_e(P_n)$ denote its extended irregular domination number. **Path-domination conjecture.** For $n\geq 4$,

$$
\gamma_e(P_n)=\begin{cases}\left\lceil\frac{n+1}{2}\right\rceil&\text{if }n=6,10,\\left\lceil\frac{n+3}{2}\right\rceil&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

The equality is known for $n\in[4,26]\setminus\{6,10\}$, while the source establishes the exceptional lower value at $n=6,10$; the asserted formula for all $n\geq 4$ remains open.

record.title: Conjecture on Ehrhart quasipolynomials of half-integral polygons
record.statement:
Let $i\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$ be the number of interior lattice points of a half-integral polygon, and require the polygon to have at least $2$ boundary lattice points. An **Ehrhart quasipolynomial enumeration conjecture.** There are exactly

$$
\frac{9}{2}i^3+36i^2+\frac{175}{2}i+53
$$

Ehrhart quasipolynomials of such half-integral polygons. The authors verified the formula through $i=16$; its validity for all $i\geq 2$ remains open.

record.title: The exceptional-group count conjecture for groups of order $p^6$
record.statement:
Let $p\geq 5$ be prime, and let an exceptional group be a finite group $G$ having a normal subgroup $N$ such that $\mu(G/N)>\mu(G)$, where $\mu(G)$ is the least integer $n$ for which $G$ embeds in the symmetric group $S_n$. The groups under consideration have order $p^6$. **Exceptional-group count conjecture.** The number of exceptional groups of order $p^6$ for primes $p\geq 5$ is

$$
\frac{11p+107}{2}.
$$

The authors identify this many groups and prove that the proportion of exceptional groups of order $p^6$ tends asymptotically to $0$ as $p$ grows. Computations for $5\leq p\leq 13$ give precisely this value, but the absence of further exceptional groups for all primes $p\geq 5$ remains conjectural.
record.source_name: E. A. O'Brien, Sunil Kumar Prajapati and Ayush Udeep, “Exceptional groups of order p^6 for primes p5”, arXiv:2410.17902 (2024).

record.title: The Futaki upper-bound conjecture for toric Calabi–Yau threefolds
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a toric Calabi–Yau $3$-fold with no factors of $\mathbb{C}$, let $\zeta_R$ be the Reeb symmetry, let $\zeta_p$ be the grading symmetry from GLSM-field degrees, and let $\eta_h$ be the test symmetry associated with a generator $x_h$. **Futaki upper-bound conjecture.** 
$$
F(\mathcal{X},\zeta_p,\eta_h)\leq \frac{8}{27}F(\mathcal{X},\zeta_R,\eta_h).
$$
 The inequality was observed for the 16 reflexive polygons and is proposed for all toric Calabi–Yau threefolds without a factor of $\mathbb{C}$; its general validity is open.
record.source_name: Jiakang Bao, Eugene Choi, Yang-Hui He, Rak-Kyeong Seong and Shing-Tung Yau, “Futaki Invariants and Reflexive Polygons”, arXiv:2410.18476 (2024).

record.title: The divisor-volume lower bound for Futaki invariants
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a toric Calabi–Yau $3$-fold with no factors of $\mathbb{C}$, let $\zeta_R$ be the Reeb symmetry, and let $\eta_h$ be the test symmetry associated with a generator $x_h$. For a toric divisor $\Sigma_\alpha$, let $V(b^*;\Sigma_\alpha)$ denote its volume at the minimizing Reeb vector. **Divisor-volume Futaki bound.** 
$$
F(\mathcal{X};\zeta_R,\eta_h)\geq \frac{27}{64}V(b^*;\Sigma_\alpha).
$$
 This bound is observed for the 16 reflexive polygons and is proposed for all toric Calabi–Yau threefolds without a factor of $\mathbb{C}$; the general case remains open.

record.title: The Laurent-coefficient lower bound for Futaki invariants
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a toric Calabi–Yau $3$-fold with no factors of $\mathbb{C}$, let $\zeta_R$ be the Reeb symmetry, and let $\eta_h$ be the test symmetry associated with a generator $x_h$. Let $A_2(\zeta_R)$ and $A_3(\zeta_R)$ be the corresponding coefficients in the Laurent expansion of the Hilbert series. **Laurent-coefficient Futaki bound.** 
$$
F(\mathcal{X};\zeta_R,\eta_h)\geq \frac{3}{8}\bigl(A_2(\zeta_R)-A_3(\zeta_R)\bigr).
$$
 The inequality is established empirically for the 16 reflexive polygons and conjectured for all toric Calabi–Yau threefolds without a factor of $\mathbb{C}$; its general validity remains open.

record.title: Erdős's squarefree-plus-power-of-two conjecture
record.statement:
Let $n>1$ be an odd integer. A **squarefree integer** is an integer not divisible by the square of any prime.

**Erdős's conjecture.** There exist a squarefree integer $m$ and an integer $k$ such that

$$
n=m+2^k.
$$

The conjecture concerns representing every odd integer greater than one as the sum of a squarefree integer and a power of two. It has been verified numerically for all odd integers up to $2^{50}$ in the source paper, extending earlier computations up to $10^7$ and $1.4\cdot 10^9$; a general proof remains open.
record.source_name: Christian Hercher, “On the Sum of Squarefree Integers and a Power of Two”, arXiv:2411.01964 (2024).

record.title: A four-term representation by pentagonal quadratic polynomials
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb N$ denote the nonnegative integers. **Four-term pentagonal representation conjecture.** Every integer $n>51$ can be written as

$$
n=\frac{w(5w-1)}2+\frac{x(5x-1)}2+\frac{y(5y+1)}2+\frac{z(5z+1)}2
$$

with $w,x,y,z\in\mathbb N$.

This is an explicit eventual universality claim analogous to Lagrange’s four-square theorem, with nonnegative variables and two signs in the linear terms. No resolution is stated in the source.
record.source_name: Zhi-Wei Sun, “New results similar to Lagrange's four-square theorem”, arXiv:2411.14308 (2024).

record.title: Eventual universality for four signed pentagonal forms
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb N$ denote the nonnegative integers and define

$$
N(1)=114862,\qquad N(-1)=166897,\qquad N(3)=196987,\qquad N(-3)=273118.
$$

**Signed pentagonal universality conjecture.** For each $r\in\{\pm1,\pm3\}$, every integer $n>N(r)$ can be written as

$$
n=\frac{x(5x+r)}2+\frac{y(5y+r)}2+\frac{z(5z+r)}2
$$

with $x,y,z\in\mathbb N$.

The conjecture gives explicit bounds for eventual universality for four ternary sums, one for each allowed linear coefficient $r$. No resolution is given in the source.

record.title: The determinant- $p$ conjecture for twisted derivations of cyclotomic integer rings
record.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $K=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)$ be the $p$th cyclotomic field, and write $O_K=\mathbb{Z}[\zeta]$. For $\beta=\sum_{i=0}^{p-2}b_i\zeta^i\in O_K$, suppose

$$
\beta(\tau-\sigma)(\zeta)=\sum_{i=0}^{p-2}\left(\sum_{j=0}^{p-2}a_{ij}b_j\right)\zeta^i.
$$

**The determinant-$p$ conjecture.** The matrix $A=[a_{ij}]$ is a $(p-1)\times(p-1)$ matrix with determinant $p$.

The conjecture has been verified computationally for all odd primes below $100$, but remains unproved for general odd primes.
record.source_name: Praveen Manju and Rajendra Kumar Sharma, “(σ, τ)-Derivations of Number Rings with Coding Theory Applications”, arXiv:2412.03500 (2026).

record.title: Böhm–Wilking conjecture on invariant curvature cones
record.statement:
Let $n\geq 12$ and let $a\in[0,n/4]$. For a curvature operator $R\in S_B^2(\mathfrak{so}(n))$, write $\operatorname{Ric}$ for its Ricci tensor and $\operatorname{scal}$ for its scalar curvature. Define

$$
\Omega(a)=\left\{R\in S_B^2(\mathfrak{so}(n))\ \middle|\ \left(\frac{n-2}{4}+a\right)\|R\|^2\leq\frac14|\operatorname{Ric}|^2,\ \operatorname{scal}>0\right\}.
$$

**Böhm–Wilking's conjecture.** For every $a\in[0,n/4]$, the curvature cone $\Omega(a)$ is invariant under the Hamilton ODE and preserved by Ricci flow.

This conjecture proposes a family of Ricci-flow-invariant curvature conditions in dimensions $n\geq12$. The supplied text identifies it as unpublished and does not provide evidence of a resolution.

record.title: The strict-partition conjecture for Robinson–Schensted shapes
record.statement:
Let $
u=(
u_1,\ldots,
u_s)\vdash m$ be a partition with distinct parts, where $s\geq 3$. Let $\mathcal{S}_
u$ denote the set of Robinson–Schensted shapes arising from permutations with cycle type $
u$, and let $\mathcal{B}_
u$ be the corresponding combinatorial candidate set.

**Strict-partition conjecture.**
 egin{enumerate}
\item If $
u_s>1$, then $\mathcal{S}_
u=\mathcal{B}_
u$.
\item If $
u_s=1$ and $m$ is odd, then $\mathcal{S}_
u=\mathcal{B}_
u$.
\item If $
u_s=1$ and $m$ is even, then $\mathcal{B}_
u\setminus\mathcal{S}_
u=\{(m/2,m/2)\}$.
\end{enumerate}

The conjecture is a natural extension of the paper’s main theorem to strict cycle types and was verified computationally for all $n\leq 15$; its general validity remains open.
